`ElectrostaticSim` computes the capacitance matrix of a layout with Palace.
This page is the reference of its calls, of the mesh settings that every Palace
simulation shares, and of the convergence declaration that Electrostatic and
Eigenmode use. The
[capacitance guide](../../guides/capacitance-palace.qmd) runs a full study, and
[Convergence and reports](../../guides/convergence-and-reports.qmd) shows how
to declare convergence and read the result. Eigenmode has its own page,
[Palace Eigenmode](palace-eigenmode.qmd).

## The calls in order {#electrostatic-calls}

[]{#candidate-surface}These are the simulation calls of the
[First simulation](../../start/first-simulation.qmd), which ran with stock
Palace 0.18.1:

```python
sim = ElectrostaticSim()
sim.set_plan(plan.prepare())
sim.set_output_dir(Path(".artifacts/simplepad-palace") / uuid4().hex[:12])
sim.add_terminal("pad", net_id="pad")
sim.add_ground(net_id="ground")
sim.set_electrostatic(unassigned_conductor_policy="error")
sim.mesh()
sim.write_config()
handoff = sim.prepare_handoff(
    profile="direct-local",
    executable=os.environ["SCGSIM_PALACE_EXECUTABLE"],
    resources={"command_style": "wrapper", "processes": 4, "threads": 1},
)
```

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| `set_plan(snapshot)` | Takes the prepared `GeometryPlan`: the geometry, the Nets, the vacuum and the Surface-EPR films. |
| `set_output_dir(path)` | The run folder the mesh, configuration and handoff are written to. |
| `add_terminal(name, net_id=...)` | Makes the conductor of one Net a terminal: a row and a column of the capacitance matrix. |
| `add_ground(net_id=...)` | Holds the conductor of one Net at 0 V. |
| `set_electrostatic(...)` | The grounding policies and saved fields; see [Defaults and grounds](#electrostatic-defaults). |
| `set_route(route, approximation_profile=None)` | Route B when not called; `set_route("A")` uses the `thin_film` profile. Call it before `mesh()`; see [Physical representation](physical-representation.qmd#palace-caller-profile). |
| `set_mesh(...)` | The mesh settings; see [Mesh settings](#palace-mesh-controls). |
| `set_numerical(...)` | The FEM order, solver and adaptive-refinement (AMR) controls. |
| `set_convergence(...)` | When adaptive refinement has converged; see [the declaration](#convergence-declaration). |
| `input_summary()` | What the model will be, before any file is written. |
| `mesh()` | Builds the SGB model, checks it for fine structure, meshes it and writes `palace.msh`. |
| `write_config()` | Writes Palace's `config.json` for that mesh. |
| `prepare_handoff(profile=..., executable=..., resources=...)` | Writes the run script and the handoff; it does not start Palace. See [Execution profiles](execution-profiles.qmd). |

A setter that fails leaves everything as it was. A setter that changes a value
discards the mesh, configuration and handoff that depended on it, so run
`mesh()` and `write_config()` again.

Before the solve, the run script hands the copied `config.json` to Palace with
its `--dry-run` option. If Palace refuses the configuration, nothing is solved
and the receipt says so: its stage is `config_compatibility` and it records
that the solver was not invoked. On Slurm, Palace's output goes to
`logs/palace-<job>.log` in the run folder.

## Mesh settings {#palace-mesh-controls}

Both `ElectrostaticSim` and `EigenmodeSim` take the same mesh settings, with
the same defaults, through `set_mesh(...)`. An argument you leave out keeps its
current value. A model needs a vacuum region: `mesh()` refuses a plan with
none, before it writes any file.

Before the mesher starts, `mesh()` runs the meshing stage of `simulation_drc`
on the model it built. A finding that refuses raises
`scgsim.palace.SimulationDrcError`, with each finding's place, owner and fix,
and no mesh is made; warnings do not stop it. The classes and limits are in
[What the meshing stage reports](../../guides/check-a-layout.qmd#what-the-meshing-stage-reports).

::: {.askr-table-compact}
| Setting | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `recipe` | `FeatureRecipe()` | How large the elements start: `FeatureRecipe`, `GlobalSizeRecipe`, `UniformBoundaryRecipe` or `GmshDefaultRecipe` ([below](#palace-mesh-recipes)). |
| `mesher` | `MesherOptions()` | Gmsh's algorithms and the order of the delivered mesh: `algorithm_2d` (Gmsh's own when `None`), `algorithm_3d` (Delaunay), `geometry_order` (1) and `high_order_optimize` (`True`). |
| `budgets` | `Budgets()` | When the repair of bad elements gives up: after 8 rounds (`max_rounds`), above 2,000,000 tetrahedra (`max_tetrahedra`), or after 180 s (`time_limit_seconds`) for a model of up to 4 mm² (`time_reference_area_mm2`), longer in proportion for a larger one. `time_target_seconds` (60 s, scaled the same way) is reported, not enforced. |
| `quality_threshold` | `0.01` | The lowest element quality accepted: the minimum signed inverse condition number, minSICN, of every tetrahedron ([what it measures](mesh-quality.qmd#audit)). |
:::

Import the recipes, `MesherOptions`, `Budgets` and the `DELAUNAY` and `HXT`
algorithm constants from `scgsim.meshing`.

::: {.callout-important title="A mesh below the quality threshold stops the run"}
`mesh()` raises `scgsim.meshing.MeshRepairError`, with the quality report,
and returns no mesh when:

- the repair rounds cannot bring every tetrahedron up to `quality_threshold`;
- the mesh needs more than `max_tetrahedra`, or the time limit is reached;
- the number of bad elements has not fallen below its lowest for two rounds
  in a row (`stalled`);
- the accepted mesh cannot be raised to `geometry_order`, or Gmsh makes no
  mesh.

**What to do.** Read where the bad elements are; the report is in the run's
`mesh/` folder, with the last mesh as a `.rejected.msh` file. A stall usually
points at geometry no mesh can repair, such as an edge or a face one grid step
wide: fix it in the layout. Otherwise choose a recipe that sizes that region
finer, raise `Budgets.max_rounds` or the time limit, or lower
`quality_threshold` and record the lower value with the study.
`Budgets(max_rounds=0)` meshes once without repair; a first mesh below the
threshold is still refused. Only `GmshDefaultRecipe` delivers a mesh below
the threshold.
:::

### Sizing recipes {#palace-mesh-recipes}

A recipe decides only how large the elements start. Repair, the threshold and
the report are the same for every recipe except `GmshDefaultRecipe`. Start
with `FeatureRecipe`: it sizes what the geometry calls for, and its defaults
reach the default threshold on 1 to 4 mm chips and, with Surface-EPR bands, on
a flip-chip qubit and on Route A sheets.

::: {.askr-table-compact}
| Recipe | Sizes | Parameters (defaults) |
|---|---|---|
| `FeatureRecipe` | A coarse size, the bounding-box diagonal over `max_size_divisor`, with finer elements at the edges of thin films (a multiple of the film thickness, when that is finer than half the coarse size: at the film's side walls on Route B and C, along the sheet's outline on Route A) and on every Surface-EPR band boundary ([below](#palace-mesh-band-edges)). An optional rule sizes the conductor outlines. | `max_size_divisor=20`, `gradation=1`, `film_sidewall_thickness_multiple=25`, `film_sidewall_ceiling_fraction=0.5`, `conductor_outline=False`, `conductor_edge_size_um=5`, `conductor_edge_grow_um=300`, `band_mesh_size_multiple=4` |
| `GlobalSizeRecipe` | Only the coarse size. A cheap reference that leaves flat tetrahedra at thin metal side walls, so it relies on repair rounds. | `max_size_divisor=20`, `gradation=1` |
| `UniformBoundaryRecipe` | Every curve of the model at `near_um`, growing to `far_um` over `far_um` micrometres, whatever the curve is. | `near_um=5`, `far_um=300` |
| `GmshDefaultRecipe` | Gmsh's own defaults, once, with no size limit and no repair. The mesh is delivered whatever its minSICN, which the report records; the tetrahedron and time budgets still apply. Choose it with `set_mesh(recipe=GmshDefaultRecipe())`. | None |
:::

Each recipe has a name and a version, recorded with its parameters, so a run
states which sizing rules made its mesh; see
[Version identities of a mesh](mesh-quality.qmd#version-identities).

#### Band boundary curves {#palace-mesh-band-edges}

A *band* is a strip of a surface cut into the model for Surface EPR: with
margins of 0.5 and 1.0 µm, the bands are the strips 0 to 0.5 µm and 0.5 to
1.0 µm from a gap edge, each 0.5 µm wide, and the rest of the face lies beyond
them. `FeatureRecipe` sizes the elements
on each band boundary at `band_mesh_size_multiple` times the narrowest band
width of its face, rounded down to the coarse size over a power of two. With
those margins the default of 4 asks for 2 µm and gets 1.1 to 2.0 µm,
depending on the model's extent. A model without bands has no band boundaries,
and the multiple changes nothing.

Keep the default of 4. A smaller multiple (2) gives better-shaped elements at
the bands but about twice the tetrahedra, and the banded flip-chip qubit then
does not mesh within the time limit. A larger multiple (8) saves elements only
where band boundaries set the size, and on Route A brings the pad's minSICN
close to the default threshold. Set another with
`set_mesh(recipe=FeatureRecipe(band_mesh_size_multiple=...))`.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="The measured multiples"}
Measured with Gmsh 4.15.2, the default threshold and budgets, one model at a
time on an otherwise lightly loaded 64-core workstation (Gmsh uses one thread);
the rows of 2 were measured beside other work. On a busy machine the same runs
took up to half as long again.

::: {.askr-table-compact}
| Multiple | Flip-chip qubit with bands | Single-die pad on Route A with bands | 1 to 4 mm chips with bands |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 1.39 million tetrahedra; stopped at the time limit | clean; 216,000 to 235,000 tetrahedra; 14 s | clean; 23,000 to 37,000 tetrahedra; 1.6 to 2.0 s |
| 4 (default) | clean in the first mesh; 569,325 tetrahedra; 53 s | clean; 89,000 to 115,000 tetrahedra; 4.7 to 5.5 s | clean; 13,000 to 20,000 tetrahedra; 1.0 to 1.2 s |
| 8 | clean after one repair round; 407,093 tetrahedra; 105 s | clean; 49,000 to 52,000 tetrahedra; 2.6 to 2.7 s | clean; 9,000 to 14,000 tetrahedra; 0.7 to 0.8 s |
| No size on band boundary curves, for comparison | clean after one repair round; 407,093 tetrahedra; 83 s | stalls at minSICN 0.003 to 0.004 | clean; 9,600 to 13,500 tetrahedra; 0.7 to 0.8 s |
:::

The flip-chip qubit is the OrcaPen SC PDK `disk_flip_chip_qubit` under common
ground planes, Route B; the pad is `square_pad_capacitor` (200 µm pad, 1 mm
die). Bands are 0.5 and 1 µm on every metal-air, metal-substrate and
substrate-air face. The cases and every run are in the
[band-edge measurement](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/scgsim/blob/develop/experiments/meshing-benchmark/band_edge.md).
The pad on Route A was measured before the outline of a Route A sheet was
sized (`scgsim.meshing.features/2`); a Route A mesh now has finer elements
along the sheet edges.
:::

### Mesher options {#palace-mesh-mesher}

`MesherOptions` sets how Gmsh meshes, whatever the sizes. Delaunay is the
default 3D algorithm; `scgsim.meshing.HXT` is the other. Meshing runs on one
thread.

`geometry_order` is the polynomial order of the delivered mesh, separate from
the FEM order of `set_numerical(order=...)`. The quality check and the repair
always work on the linear mesh. Above 1, the accepted mesh is raised to that
order, optionally smoothed once by Gmsh's `HighOrder` optimisation
(`high_order_optimize`), and written. If the curved elements cannot be made,
`mesh()` fails; it never substitutes a straight or lower-order mesh.

### What `mesh()` writes {#palace-mesh-outputs}

The run folder holds the SGB model (`geometry/`), the meshing report (`mesh/`,
as JSON and as text; see [The quality report](mesh-quality.qmd#quality-report)),
`palace.msh` (Gmsh MSH 2.2, the format Palace reads) and the mesh manifest
(`metadata/`). Each Terminal and Ground binds to the exact Net of the model.

### Mesh summary {#mesh-manifest-and-detached-summary}

`sim.mesh_summary()`, and the same call on a resolved run, returns the mesh's
settings, its node, element and region counts, its order and edge lengths. For
Eigenmode it adds an estimate of the degrees of freedom, from the mesh and the
FEM order; it is not Palace's count. The records it reads are in
[the internals](../../contribute/internals/report-records.qmd#mesh-manifest).

## Surface-EPR margins {#surface-epr-margins}

Electrostatic reads the same Surface-EPR specs as Eigenmode, set on the plan
with `plan.set_surface_epr(specs)` before `prepare()`; the
[Eigenmode reference](palace-eigenmode.qmd#surface-epr-margins) gives their
keys and rows. A plan without specs gets no bands and no Surface-EPR rows.

## Convergence declaration {#convergence-declaration}

`set_convergence(*criteria, minimum_converged_passes=1)` declares when an
adaptive run has converged. `ElectrostaticSim` and `EigenmodeSim` take it;
`DrivenSim` refuses it until S-parameters have a convergence quantity. A
criterion is a quantity and a threshold; no threshold has a default:

```python
from scgsim.palace import Capacitance, ErrorIndicator, SurfaceEpr

sim.set_numerical(order=2, amr_max_passes=12)
sim.set_convergence(
    Capacitance.diagonal().within(percent=0.1),
    Capacitance.element("island", "resonator").within(percent=1),
    SurfaceEpr.each("MA", "MS", "SA", margin_um=1.0).within(percent=2),
    ErrorIndicator().below(1e-2),
    minimum_converged_passes=2,
)
```

The numbers only show the form; the thresholds are yours.

| Quantity | On | Each pass reads |
|---|---|---|
| `Capacitance.element(a, b)`, `.diagonal()`, `.sub_diagonal(offset=1)`, `.off_diagonal()`, `.matrix()`, `.elements([(a, b), ...])` | `ElectrostaticSim` | Elements `C[a][b]` of the Maxwell matrix in `terminal-C.csv`, named by terminal. `sub_diagonal` pairs terminals `offset` apart in the order they were added; `off_diagonal` and `matrix` take each pair of different terminals once. |
| `ModeFrequency(modes=None)` | `EigenmodeSim` | `Re{f}` of each selected mode in `eig.csv`, in GHz; `None` selects every computed mode. |
| `SurfaceEpr(interface_kind, margin_um=None, modes=None, terminals=None)` | both | The participation of one interface type: the sum over its whole-surface rows, or over its margin rows at `margin_um`. One number per mode (`modes=`, Eigenmode) or per excitation (`terminals=`, Electrostatic); `None` selects all. `SurfaceEpr.each("MA", "MS", "SA")` declares one criterion per type with one threshold. |
| `ErrorIndicator()` | both | The `Norm` Palace writes to `error-indicators.csv`. |

`within(percent=p)` bounds the change from the previous pass as a percentage
of the value, $100\,|q_k - q_{k-1}| / |q_k|$: the measure AEDT reports as
`Delta %` for a Q3D matrix and `Max Delta Freq. %` for HFSS Eigenmode. When
$q_k$ is zero the change is zero if $q_{k-1}$ is zero too, and otherwise
undefined, so the criterion does not hold. The absolute form names the unit
the quantity is stored in: `absolute_f` for capacitance (farads),
`absolute_ghz` for frequency, `absolute` for a participation, which has no
unit. Give exactly one. `ErrorIndicator().below(value)` bounds the value
itself.

A pass is one Palace solve: pass 1 solves the input mesh, and pass $k$ follows
$k-1$ refinements. A change criterion compares pass $k$ with pass $k-1$, so it
cannot hold at pass 1. A quantity with several numbers holds when each of them
does. The run has converged at pass $k$ when every criterion holds at each of
the `minimum_converged_passes` passes ending at $k$. A margin row is a part of
its whole-surface row, so the two are never added.

::: {.callout-note title="Declare Surface EPR beyond a margin"}
A change criterion says that a quantity moved little between two passes, not
how far it is from its limit. On the layouts SCGSim has measured, whole-surface
participation grew at every pass and no change criterion on it held, so such a
run goes to its pass limit. Participation beyond a margin (`margin_um=`)
settled, though not steadily from pass to pass, which is what
`minimum_converged_passes` is for. Put Surface-EPR criteria on a margin. The
measurements are recorded
[here](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/scgsim/issues/248#issuecomment-6873586635).
:::

Another call replaces the whole declaration; `set_convergence(None)` removes
it, and `set_convergence()` with no criterion is refused. The call keeps the
mesh and discards the configuration and handoff, as `set_numerical` does.

### Checks {#checks}

`set_convergence` refuses, naming the call to change:

- a quantity the simulation does not take (a `Capacitance` on `EigenmodeSim`,
  a `ModeFrequency` on `ElectrostaticSim`, `modes=` on Electrostatic or
  `terminals=` on Eigenmode);
- a threshold that is not positive and finite, two thresholds, or none;
- `minimum_converged_passes` that is not a whole number of at least 1.

`write_config()` refuses, before it writes anything:

- a terminal name the simulation does not have, or a selection with no element;
- a mode beyond `num_modes`;
- an interface type with no Surface EPR on the plan, or one that
  `set_epr_request(surface_interfaces=...)` leaves out;
- a `margin_um` its spec does not declare, naming the margins it does;
- an `amr_max_passes` too small for the declaration to hold: a run of
  `amr_max_passes` refinements solves `amr_max_passes + 1` times, and the
  declaration needs `minimum_converged_passes` solves, plus one when a
  criterion is on a change;
- a stated `amr_tolerance` (declare `ErrorIndicator().below(...)` instead);
- `save_adapt_iterations=False`, since every pass is read.

### What is written {#what-is-written-and-how-it-relates-to-the-amr-controls}

With a declaration, your criteria take the place of Palace's own tolerance:
`write_config()` sets it so that only `amr_max_passes` ends Palace, and has
Palace keep every pass in `results/palace/iteration<k>`. The criteria are
written to `metadata/palace_convergence_plan.json` and sealed with the
handoff, so a returned run whose plan changed is refused. Without a
declaration, the configuration is what the AMR controls alone give. The
record's contents are in
[the internals](../../contribute/internals/report-records.qmd#convergence-plan-record).

### The stop at convergence {#convergence-stop}

With a declaration, the run script stops Palace once the criteria have
converged, one to two seconds after the pass at which they hold, so the passes
after it are not solved. The run still ends as completed, and its result is
that last pass. A pass shorter than those one to two seconds still runs; the
verdict then names how many passes were read after the one that converged.

The receipt records how Palace ended (`ending`):

| `ending` | When | Run |
|---|---|---|
| `solver_ended` | Palace ended by itself | completed when every exit code is 0 |
| `stopped_at_convergence` | SCGSim stopped it after a converged pass | completed |
| `stop_escalated`, `runner_terminated`, `not_recorded` | The stop did not finish cleanly, or the run was ended from outside | failed |

Result reading checks the returned files against the runner's decision record
and the receipt, and refuses a folder where they disagree.
`ResolvedPalaceResult.convergence` and the
[trust report](report-model.qmd#declared-convergence) say at which pass the
run converged and where Palace stopped; `ResolvedPalaceResult.solver_end` holds
the receipt's `ending`. How the runner watches and stops Palace is in
[the internals](../../contribute/internals/report-records.qmd#convergence-runner).

## Defaults and grounds {#electrostatic-defaults}

[]{#candidate-electrostatic-defaults}`ElectrostaticSim` starts with these
values; they are defaults of the implementation, not recommendations:

| Setting | Default |
|---|---|
| `save_fields` | `0` |
| `unassigned_conductor_policy` | `"ground"` |
| `exterior_boundary_policy` | `"none"` |
| `Model.Refinement.Nonconformal` | `false` unless you set `amr_nonconformal=True` |
| `Model.Refinement.SaveAdaptMesh` | not written unless you set `save_adapt_mesh=True` or `False` |
| AMR | 0 passes, conformal, tolerance 0.01 |

Palace itself defaults `Nonconformal` to `true`; SCGSim always writes the key
and defaults it to `false`. `set_numerical(save_adapt_mesh=...)` takes `True`,
`False` or `None` (leave the key out). Read the settings back with
`sim.numerical`, a `NumericalControls` (`sim.numerical.amr_nonconformal`;
`to_payload()` gives the dictionary in `metadata/palace_numerical_controls.json`),
and the plan's films with `sim.surface_epr_specs`. With a
[convergence declaration](#convergence-declaration) the default tolerance is
set aside and a stated one is refused.

**Grounds.** A conductor that is neither a terminal nor a ground is grounded by
default (`unassigned_conductor_policy="ground"`). With
`unassigned_conductor_policy="error"`, as in the example at the top, every
conductor must be a terminal or a ground: there the pad is the terminal, and
the ground Net is held at 0 V by `add_ground`. `add_ground(net_id=...)`
grounds a real conductor; `exterior_boundary_policy="ground"` grounds the outer
faces of the model instead, and the two are recorded apart.

[]{#source-and-geometry-authority}The simulation's geometry comes only from the
plan it is given; [GeometryPlan and SGB](geometry-plan.qmd) is its reference.
